tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?

options.A: He is going to leave his present job.
options.B: He is going to attend a job interview.
options.C: He will meet his new manager in two weeks.
options.D: He will tell the management how he really feels.

questions.cn: 从对话中关于男士我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他即将辞去现在的工作。
optionsCn.B: 他将去参加一场求职面试。
optionsCn.C: 他两周后会见他的新经理。
optionsCn.D: 他会告诉管理层自己的真实感受。

questions.stem: What does the woman think about the information gained from an exit interview?

options.A: It should be carefully analyzed.
options.B: It should be kept private.
options.C: It can be quite useful to senior managers.
options.D: It can improve interviewees' job prospects.

questions.cn: 女士如何看待离职面谈中获得的信息？

optionsCn.A: 它应被仔细分析。
optionsCn.B: 它应当保密。
optionsCn.C: 它对高层管理者可能相当有用。
optionsCn.D: 它能改善受访者的职业前景。

questions.stem: Why does the man want to rethink what he will say in the coming exit interview?

options.A: It may do harm to his fellow employees.
options.B: It may displease his immediate superiors.
options.C: It may adversely affect his future career prospects.
options.D: It may leave a negative impression on the interviewer.

questions.cn: 男士为什么想重新考虑即将到来的离职面谈中要说的话？

optionsCn.A: 这可能伤害他的同事。
optionsCn.B: 这可能让他的直接上级不满。
optionsCn.C: 这可能对他未来的职业前景产生不利影响。
optionsCn.D: 这可能给面试者留下负面印象。

questions.stem: What does the man think he had better do?

options.A: Pour out his frustrations on a rate-your-employer website.
options.B: Network with his close friends to find a better employer.
options.C: Do some practice for the exit interview.
options.D: Prepare a comprehensive exit report.

questions.cn: 男士认为他最好怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 在“评价你的雇主”网站上倾泻他的不满。
optionsCn.B: 与好友建立人脉以找到更好的雇主。
optionsCn.C: 为离职面谈做些练习。
optionsCn.D: 准备一份全面的离职报告。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: It's my last day at work tomorrow.
lines.cn: M：明天是我上班的最后一天。

lines.t: M: I start my new job in two weeks.
lines.cn: M：两周后我去新岗位上岗。

lines.t: M: My human resources manager wants to conduct an interview with me before I leave.
lines.cn: M：我的人力资源经理希望在我离职前和我做一次面谈。

lines.t: F: Ah, an exit interview.
lines.cn: F：啊，离职面谈。

lines.t: F: Are you looking forward to it?
lines.cn: F：你期待吗？

lines.t: M: I'm not sure how I feel about it.
lines.cn: M：我说不清自己是什么感受。

lines.t: M: I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time, but I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel.
lines.cn: M：我辞职是因为那家公司让我不开心很久了，但我不确定要不要告诉他们我的真实感受。

lines.t: F: To my way of thinking, there are two main potential benefits that come from unleashing an agitated stream of truth during an exit interview.
lines.cn: F：按我的想法，在离职面谈中把一肚子实话倾泻出来，主要有两方面的潜在好处。

lines.t: F: The first is release.
lines.cn: F：第一是释放。

lines.t: F: Unburdening yourself of frustration and perhaps even anger to someone who isn't a friend or close colleague can be wonderfully freeing.
lines.cn: F：向一个并非朋友或亲近同事的人卸下沮丧甚至愤怒，会带来奇妙的解脱感。

lines.t: M: And let me guess, the second is that the criticism will, theoretically, help the organization I'm leaving to improve, making sure employees of the future are less likely to encounter what I did?
lines.cn: M：让我猜猜，第二是这些批评理论上会帮助我即将离开的机构改进，确保将来的员工不太可能遇到我遇到的情况？

lines.t: F: That's right, but the problem with the company improvement part is that very often it doesn't happen.
lines.cn: F：对，但公司改进这一部分的问题在于，它往往并不会发生。

lines.t: F: An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't.
lines.cn: F：离职面谈本应是保密的，但常常并非如此。

lines.t: F: In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential and the information is used as dirt against another manager or it can be traded among senior managers.
lines.cn: F：在我公司，从这类面谈中得到的信息往往不保密，还会被当作黑料用来攻击另一位管理者，或在高层管理者之间交易。

lines.t: M: Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose in the interview.
lines.cn: M：现在你让我得重新考虑面谈时该说什么了。

lines.t: M: There is always the chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry.
lines.cn: M：这总有可能影响我的名声以及我在行业内建立人脉的能力。

lines.t: M: It is a pretty small industry after all.
lines.cn: M：毕竟这个行业相当小。

lines.t: F: Anything you initially gain from the instant satisfaction of telling it like it is, you might lose down the track by injuring your future career prospects.
lines.cn: F：你最初从“实话实说”的即时快感中得到的一切，日后都可能因损害你未来的职业前景而失去。

lines.t: M: Right, perhaps I would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate your employer websites.
lines.cn: M：对，也许我去那种“评价你的雇主”的网站把心里话说出来会更好。

lines.t: F: You could, and don't do the interview at all.
lines.cn: F：你可以那样做，干脆不参加这次面谈。

lines.t: F: Exit interviews are not mandatory.
lines.cn: F：离职面谈并非强制性的。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the man want Jane Forrester to talk about?

options.A: Her career as a botanist.
options.B: Her latest documentary.
options.C: Her month-long expedition.
options.D: Her unsuccessful journey.

questions.cn: 男士想让简·福斯特谈什么？

optionsCn.A: 她作为植物学家的职业生涯。
optionsCn.B: 她最新的纪录片。
optionsCn.C: 她为期一个月的考察。
optionsCn.D: 她不成功的旅行。

questions.stem: Why does the woman describe her experience as far from glamorous?

options.A: She was caught in a hurricane.
options.B: She had to live like a vegetarian.
options.C: She suffered from water shortage.
options.D: She had to endure many hardships.

questions.cn: 女士为什么说她的经历一点也不光鲜？

optionsCn.A: 她遭遇了飓风。
optionsCn.B: 她不得不像素食者一样生活。
optionsCn.C: 她遭遇缺水。
optionsCn.D: 她不得不忍受许多艰苦。

questions.stem: Why did the woman and those who went with her end their trip halfway?

options.A: They could no longer bear the humidity.
options.B: They had no more food in the canoe.
options.C: A flood was approaching.
options.D: A hurricane was coming.

questions.cn: 女士和同行的人为什么在行程中途结束了旅行？

optionsCn.A: 他们再也受不了那种湿度。
optionsCn.B: 独木舟上没有食物了。
optionsCn.C: 洪水正在逼近。
optionsCn.D: 飓风即将来临。

questions.stem: What does the woman think of Jane Forrester?

options.A: It was memorable.
options.B: It was unbearable.
options.C: It was fruitful.
options.D: It was uneventful.

questions.cn: 女士对简·福斯特之行怎么看？

optionsCn.A: 它令人难忘。
optionsCn.B: 它令人难以忍受。
optionsCn.C: 它富有成果。
optionsCn.D: 它平淡无奇。

lines.t: Conversation two
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: Today I'm talking to the renowned botanist Jane Forster.
lines.cn: M：今天我要和著名植物学家简·福斯特聊聊。

lines.t: F: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry.
lines.cn: F：谢谢你邀请我来上节目，亨利。

lines.t: M: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary.
lines.cn: M：简，你最新的纪录片发布之后，最近可是成了名人。

lines.t: M: Can you tell us a little about it?
lines.cn: M：能跟我们讲讲吗？

lines.t: F: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest in equatorial areas of Southeast Asia.
lines.cn: F：好的，它记录了我去研究东南亚赤道地区雨林原生植被的考察。

lines.t: M: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations.
lines.cn: M：你确实去过一些非常异域的地方。

lines.t: F: It was far from glamorous, to be honest.
lines.cn: F：说实话，那一点都不光鲜。

lines.t: F: The area we visited was accessible only by canoe, and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least.
lines.cn: F：我们去的地方只能划独木舟进入，小屋里的居住条件至少可以说是原始的。

lines.t: F: There was no electricity, and our water supply was a nearby stream.
lines.cn: F：没有电，用水取自附近的小溪。

lines.t: M: How were the weather conditions while you were there?
lines.cn: M：你们在那儿时天气怎么样？

lines.t: F: The weather was not conducive to our work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable.
lines.cn: F：天气完全不利于我们的工作，因为湿度几乎让人受不了。

lines.t: F: At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing.
lines.cn: F：中午我们就待在小屋里，什么也做不了。

lines.t: F: It was too humid to either work or sleep.
lines.cn: F：湿得既没法工作也没法睡觉。

lines.t: M: How long did your team spend in the jungle?
lines.cn: M：你们团队在丛林里待了多久？

lines.t: F: Originally, we planned to be there for a month, but in the end, we stayed for only two weeks.
lines.cn: F：原本我们计划待一个月，但最后只待了两周。

lines.t: M: Why did you cut the expedition short?
lines.cn: M：为什么缩短了考察？

lines.t: F: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching, and we had to evacuate at very short notice.
lines.cn: F：行程过半时，我们收到消息说有飓风逼近，不得不在极短的时间内撤离。

lines.t: M: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote.
lines.cn: M：听起来是段很精彩的轶事。

lines.t: F: It was frightening.
lines.cn: F：那很可怕。

lines.t: F: The fastest evacuation route was through river rapids.
lines.cn: F：最快的撤离路线要穿过河中急流。

lines.t: F: We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment.
lines.cn: F：我们得带着全部设备在里面航行。

lines.t: M: So overall, was the journey unsuccessful?
lines.cn: M：那么总的说来，这次旅程是不成功的？

lines.t: F: Absolutely not.
lines.cn: F：绝对不是。

lines.t: F: We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.
lines.cn: F：我们收集了大量关于当地植物生命的数据。

lines.t: M: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions?
lines.cn: M：你为什么能忍受这样恶劣的条件？

lines.t: F: Botany is an obsession for me.
lines.cn: F：植物学让我着迷。

lines.t: F: Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery, and I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world.
lines.cn: F：我去的许多目的地都有令人惊叹的景色，我还能遇到来自世界各地的各种人。

lines.t: M: So where will your next destination be?
lines.cn: M：那你下一个目的地是哪里？

lines.t: F: I haven't decided yet.
lines.cn: F：我还没决定。

lines.t: M: Then we can leave it for another occasion.
lines.cn: M：那我们就留到下次再说。

lines.t: F: Thanks.
lines.cn: F：谢谢。

lines.t: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
lines.cn: 从这段对话中，关于男士我们了解到什么？

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the use of jargon terms by experts?

options.A: It ensures the accuracy of their arguments.
options.B: It diminishes laymen's interest in science.
options.C: It hurts laymen's dignity and self-esteem.
options.D: It makes their expressions more explicit.

questions.cn: 文章说专家使用术语带来了什么影响？

optionsCn.A: 它确保了他们论点的准确性。
optionsCn.B: 它削弱了普通人对科学的兴趣。
optionsCn.C: 它伤害了普通人的尊严和自尊。
optionsCn.D: 它让他们的表达更清楚。

questions.stem: What do researchers find about people reading scientific articles containing jargon terms?

options.A: They will see the complexity of science.
options.B: They feel great respect towards scientists.
options.C: They tend to disbelieve the actual science.
options.D: They can learn to communicate with scientists.

questions.cn: 研究者发现，读含术语科学文章的人会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 他们会看到科学的复杂性。
optionsCn.B: 他们对科学家怀有极大敬意。
optionsCn.C: 他们倾向于不相信那门科学本身。
optionsCn.D: 他们能学会与科学家交流。

questions.stem: What does Shulman suggest scientists do when communicating with the general public?

options.A: Explain all the jargon terms.
options.B: Do away with jargon terms.
options.C: Find appropriate topics.
options.D: Stimulate their interest.

questions.cn: 舒尔曼建议科学家与公众沟通时怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 解释所有术语。
optionsCn.B: 取消术语。
optionsCn.C: 寻找合适的话题。
optionsCn.D: 激发他们的兴趣。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Readers felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics.
lines.cn: 读者感到对科学的了解更少，也更没资格谈论科学话题。

lines.t: It's noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text.
lines.cn: 值得注意的是，术语在文中是否被解释，并没有造成差别。

lines.t: Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn't explained.
lines.cn: 即使术语有解释，读者仍感到和读那些没有解释的术语时一样的疏离。

lines.t: The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers.
lines.cn: 问题在于，光是有术语存在，就向读者发出了令人泄气的信号。

lines.t: Hilary Shulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialised words are a signal.
lines.cn: 该研究的作者希拉里·舒尔曼断言，专业词汇是一种信号。

lines.t: Jargon tells people that the message isn't for them.
lines.cn: 术语告诉人们：这条信息不是给你们的。

lines.t: There's an even darker side to how people react to jargon.
lines.cn: 人们对术语的反应还有更阴暗的一面。

lines.t: In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science.
lines.cn: 在另一项研究中，研究者发现，阅读含有术语的科学文章会让人怀疑那门科学本身。

lines.t: They found the opposite when a text is easier to read.
lines.cn: 而当文本更易读时，他们发现了相反的结果。

lines.t: Then, people are more persuaded.
lines.cn: 那时，人们更容易被说服。

lines.t: Thus, it's important to communicate clearly when talking about complex science subjects.
lines.cn: 因此，谈论复杂的科学话题时，表述清晰很重要。

lines.t: This is especially true with issues related to public health, like the safety of new medications and the benefits of vaccines.
lines.cn: 在涉及公共卫生的问题上尤其如此，比如新药的安全性和疫苗的益处。

lines.t: Shulman concedes that the use of jargon is appropriate with scientific audiences.
lines.cn: 舒尔曼承认，面对科学界受众时使用术语是恰当的。

lines.t: But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language.
lines.cn: 但想与公众沟通的科学家需要调整自己的语言。

lines.t: They need to eliminate jargon.
lines.cn: 他们需要消除术语。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did Texas businessman Petilio Higgins believe?

options.A: There were oil deposits below a local gassy hill.
options.B: The erupting gas might endanger local children.
options.C: There was oil leakage along the Gulf Coast.
options.D: The local gassy hill might start a huge fire.

questions.cn: 得克萨斯商人帕蒂奥·希金斯相信什么？

optionsCn.A: 当地一座冒气的小山下面有石油矿藏。
optionsCn.B: 喷出的气体可能危及当地儿童。
optionsCn.C: 墨西哥湾沿岸有石油泄漏。
optionsCn.D: 当地冒气的小山可能引发大火。

questions.stem: What prevented Higgins' workers from digging a proper hole to get the oil?

options.A: The massive gas underground.
options.B: Their lack of the needed skill.
options.C: Their lack of suitable tools.
options.D: The sand under the hill.

questions.cn: 是什么让希金斯的工人无法挖出合适的孔洞取油？

optionsCn.A: 地下大量的天然气。
optionsCn.B: 他们缺乏必要的技能。
optionsCn.C: 他们缺乏合适的工具。
optionsCn.D: 山下的沙子。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Captain Lucas's drilling method?

options.A: It was not as effective as he claimed.
options.B: It rendered many oil workers jobless.
options.C: It gave birth to the oil drilling industry.
options.D: It was not popularized until years later.

questions.cn: 关于卢卡斯上尉的钻探方法，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它并不像他声称的那样有效。
optionsCn.B: 它使许多石油工人失业。
optionsCn.C: 它催生了石油钻探业。
optionsCn.D: 它多年后才被推广。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Texas' oil industry boom?

options.A: It ruined the state's cotton and beef industries.
options.B: It totally destroyed the state's rural landscape.
options.C: It resulted in an oil surplus all over the world.
options.D: It radically transformed the state's economy.

questions.cn: 关于得克萨斯的石油业繁荣，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它毁掉了该州的棉花和牛肉产业。
optionsCn.B: 它彻底破坏了该州的乡村景观。
optionsCn.C: 它导致全世界石油过剩。
optionsCn.D: 它彻底改变了该州的经济。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: At the beginning of the 20th century, on the Gulf Coast in the U.
lines.cn: 20 世纪初，在美国

lines.t: S.
lines.cn: 得

lines.t: state of Texas, there was a hill where gas leakage was so noticeable that schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire.
lines.cn: 克萨斯州墨西哥湾沿岸，有一座小山，那里天然气泄漏非常明显，以至于学童有时会把小山点着。

lines.t: Patio Higgins, a disreputable local businessman, became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill.
lines.cn: 帕蒂奥·希金斯，一位名声不佳的当地商人，确信这座冒气的小山下面有石油。

lines.t: Oil wells weren't drilled back then.
lines.cn: 那时还不打油井。

lines.t: They were essentially dug.
lines.cn: 基本上是挖井。

lines.t: The sand under the hill defeated several attempts by Higgins' workers to make a proper hole.
lines.cn: 山下的沙子让希金斯的工人几次尝试挖出一个像样的孔洞都失败了。

lines.t: Higgins had forecast oil at a thousand feet, a totally made-up figure.
lines.cn: 希金斯预测在 1000 英尺处有石油，这个数字完全是编出来的。

lines.t: Higgins subsequently hired a mining engineer, Captain Anthony Lucas.
lines.cn: 希金斯随后聘了一位采矿工程师安东尼·卢卡斯上尉。

lines.t: After encountering several setbacks, Captain Lucas decided to use a drill, and his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry.
lines.cn: 在遭遇数次挫折之后，卢卡斯上尉决定使用钻机，他的创新缔造了现代石油钻探业。

lines.t: In January 1901, at 1,020 feet, almost precisely the depth predicted by Higgins' wild guess, the well roared and suddenly ejected mud and six tons of drilling pipe out of the ground, terrifying those present.
lines.cn: 1901 年 1 月，在 1020 英尺处——几乎正好是希金斯胡乱猜测的深度——油井轰鸣起来，突然把泥浆和六吨重的钻杆喷出地面，吓坏了在场的人。

lines.t: For the next nine days until the well was capped, the well poured out more oil than all the wells in America combined.
lines.cn: 在接下来封井前的九天里，这口井喷出的石油比全美所有油井加起来还多。

lines.t: In those days, Texas was almost entirely rural, with no large cities and practically no industry.
lines.cn: 当时，得克萨斯几乎完全是乡村，没有大城市，也几乎没有工业。

lines.t: Cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy.
lines.cn: 棉花和牛肉是经济的基础。

lines.t: Higgins' well changed that.
lines.cn: 希金斯的油井改变了这一切。

lines.t: The boom made some prospectors millionaires, but the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas.
lines.cn: 这场繁荣让一些勘探者成了百万富翁，但石油的突然过剩对得克萨斯并不完全是好事。

lines.t: In the 1930s, prices crashed to the point that, in some parts of the country, oil was cheaper than water.
lines.cn: 20 世纪 30 年代，油价暴跌到在某些地方石油比水还便宜。

lines.t: That would become a familiar pattern of the boom-or-bust Texas economy.
lines.cn: 这后来成了得克萨斯经济“繁荣—崩溃”的常见模式。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is a primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to recent research?

options.A: Insufficient motivation.
options.B: Tough regulations.
options.C: Unsuitable jobs.
options.D: Bad managers.

questions.cn: 根据最新研究，员工不满的一个主要原因是什么？

optionsCn.A: 动力不足。
optionsCn.B: 严苛的规定。
optionsCn.C: 不合适的工作。
optionsCn.D: 糟糕的管理者。

questions.stem: What is one of the causes for poor management practices?

options.A: Ineffective training.
options.B: Toxic company culture.
options.C: Overburdening of managers.
options.D: Lack of regular evaluation.

questions.cn: 管理不善的原因之一是什么？

optionsCn.A: 无效的培训。
optionsCn.B: 有毒的公司文化。
optionsCn.C: 管理者负担过重。
optionsCn.D: 缺乏定期评估。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the study on job dissatisfaction?

options.A: It was based only on the perspective of employees.
options.B: It provided meaningful clues to solving the problem.
options.C: It was conducted from frontline managers' point of view.
options.D: It collected feedback from both employers and employees.

questions.cn: 关于这项关于工作不满的研究，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它只基于员工的视角。
optionsCn.B: 它为解决问题提供了有意义的线索。
optionsCn.C: 它是从基层管理者的角度进行的。
optionsCn.D: 它收集了雇主和员工双方的反馈。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Most people dislike their jobs.
lines.cn: 大多数人不喜欢自己的工作。

lines.t: It's an astonishing but statistical fact.
lines.cn: 这是个令人吃惊但确有统计依据的事实。

lines.t: A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers.
lines.cn: 根据最新研究，员工不满的一个主要原因是，许多人认为自己遇到了糟糕的管理者。

lines.t: Few describe their managers as malicious or manipulative, though.
lines.cn: 不过很少有人把管理者描述为恶毒或善于操控。

lines.t: While those types certainly exist, they're a minority.
lines.cn: 这类人固然存在，但只是少数。

lines.t: The majority of managers seemingly just don't know any better.
lines.cn: 大多数管理者似乎只是根本不知道该如何做得更好。

lines.t: They're often emulating bad managers they've had in the past.
lines.cn: 他们往往在效仿自己过去遇到的糟糕管理者。

lines.t: It's likely they've never read a management book or attended a management course.
lines.cn: 他们很可能从未读过管理学书籍，也没上过管理课程。

lines.t: They might not have even reflected on what good management looks like and how it would influence their own management style.
lines.cn: 他们甚至可能从未思考过什么是好的管理，以及它会如何影响自己的管理风格。

lines.t: The researchers interviewed employees about their managers, beginning with a question about the worst manager they had ever had.
lines.cn: 研究者就管理者问题采访了员工，首先问的是他们遇到过的最糟糕的管理者。

lines.t: From this, the researchers came up with four main causes of why some managers are perceived as being simply awful at their jobs.
lines.cn: 由此，研究者提出了某些管理者被认为完全不胜任工作的四大原因。

lines.t: The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices.
lines.cn: 第一个原因是公司文化，员工认为它纵容了糟糕的管理做法。

lines.t: It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training, and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy.
lines.cn: 其中被认定最该负责的是压力巨大的工作环境、极少的培训，以及缺乏问责。

lines.t: Often, a manager's superiors can effectively encourage a manager's distasteful behavior when they fail to discipline the person's wrongdoings.
lines.cn: 当管理者的上级不对其错误行为加以惩戒时，往往实际上是在鼓励这种令人反感的作风。

lines.t: Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.
lines.cn: 这样的工作场所有时被描述为“有毒”。

lines.t: The second cause was attributed to the manager's characteristics.
lines.cn: 第二个原因归因于管理者自身的特质。

lines.t: Those deemed to be most destructive were odd people, those without drive, those who allow personal problems into the workplace, and those with an unpleasant temperament or personality in general.
lines.cn: 被认为最具破坏性的是：性格古怪的人、没有干劲的人、把私人问题带进职场的人，以及总体脾气或性格令人不快的人。

lines.t: The third cause of poor management was associated with a deficiency of qualifications.
lines.cn: 管理不善的第三个原因与资历不足有关。

lines.t: Not so much the formal variety one obtains from a university, but the informal variety that comes from credible work experience and professional accomplishments.
lines.cn: 这里说的不是从大学获得的正式学历，而是来自可靠工作经验和专业成就的非正式资历。

lines.t: The fourth cause concerned managers who've been promoted for reasons other than potential.
lines.cn: 第四个原因涉及那些并非因潜力而被提拔的管理者。

lines.t: One reason in particular why these people had been promoted was that they had been around the longest.
lines.cn: 这类人被提拔的一个特别原因是：他们待的时间最长。

lines.t: It wasn't their skill set or other merits that got them the job.
lines.cn: 让他们得到这个职位的并不是技能或其他优点。

lines.t: It was their tenure.
lines.cn: 而是他们的资历年限。

lines.t: A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees.
lines.cn: 值得指出的一点是，这项研究只基于员工的视角。

lines.t: The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers.
lines.cn: 研究者没有询问高层领导如何看待他们的基层管理者。

lines.t: It's quite possible they're content with how the individuals they promoted are now performing.
lines.cn: 很可能他们对自己提拔的人现在的表现是满意的。

lines.t: Merely ignorant of the damage they're actually causing.
lines.cn: 只是不知道这些人实际造成的伤害而已。

lines.t: Which might explain why, as the researchers conclude, those same middle managers are usually unaware that they are a bad manager.
lines.cn: 这或许可以解释，正如研究者所总结的，这些中层管理者通常并不知道自己是糟糕的管理者。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the mining industry in Western Australia?

options.B: It is bringing prosperity to the region.
options.C: It is yielding an unprecedented profit.
options.D: It is seeing an automation revolution.

optionsCn.A: 它正以加速的势头扩张。
optionsCn.B: 它正在给该地区带来繁荣。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.
lines.cn: 随着无人驾驶车辆似乎不可避免，澳大利亚广袤沙漠地区西澳大利亚州的矿业公司无疑走在了前面。

lines.t: Iron ore is a key ingredient in steelmaking.
lines.cn: 铁矿石是炼钢的关键原料。

lines.t: The mining companies here produce almost 300 million tons of iron ore a year.
lines.cn: 这里的矿业公司每年生产近 3 亿吨铁矿石。

lines.t: The 240 giant autonomous trucks in use in the Western Australian mines can weigh 400 tons fully loaded and travel at speeds of up to 60 kilometers per hour.
lines.cn: 西澳矿区使用的 240 辆巨型自动驾驶卡车满载时重达 400 吨，行驶速度可达每小时 60 公里。

lines.t: They are a technological leap, transporting iron ore along routes which run for hundreds of kilometers from mines to their destinations.
lines.cn: 这是一次技术飞跃，它们沿着从矿山到目的地长达数百公里的路线运输铁矿石。

lines.t: Here, when the truck arrives at its destination, staff in the operations center direct it precisely where to unload.
lines.cn: 在这里，当卡车到达目的地时，运营中心的工作人员会精确指引它在哪里卸货。

lines.t: Vast quantities of iron ore are then transported by autonomous trains to ocean ports.
lines.cn: 随后，大量铁矿石由自动驾驶列车运往海港。

lines.t: Advocates argue these automated vehicles will change mining forever.
lines.cn: 支持者主张，这些自动化车辆将永远改变采矿业。

lines.t: It may only be five years before the use of automation technology leads to a fully robotic mine.
lines.cn: 也许只需五年，自动化技术的应用就会催生出全机器人化的矿山。

lines.t: A range of factors has pushed Western Australia's desert region to the lead of this automation revolution.
lines.cn: 一系列因素把西澳大利亚的沙漠地区推到了这场自动化革命的前列。

lines.t: These include the huge size of the mines, the scale of equipment, and the repetitive nature of some of the work.
lines.cn: 这些因素包括矿山的巨大规模、设备的体量，以及部分工作的重复性。

lines.t: Then there's the area's remoteness.
lines.cn: 再有就是这一地区的偏远。

lines.t: At 502,000 square kilometers, it can sometimes make recruiting staff a challenge.
lines.cn: 50.2 万平方公里的面积，有时会让招募员工成为难题。

lines.t: Another consideration is the risks when humans interact with large machinery.
lines.cn: 另一个考虑是人与大型机械互动时的风险。

lines.t: There are also the financial imperatives.
lines.cn: 还有财务上的必然要求。

lines.t: The ongoing push by the mining corporations to be more productive and more efficient is another powerful driver in embracing automation technology.
lines.cn: 矿业公司不断提高生产力和效率的持续追求，是拥抱自动化技术的另一大推动力。

lines.t: The concept of a fully autonomous mine is a bit of a misleading term, however.
lines.cn: 不过，“完全自主的矿山”这个概念有点误导人。

lines.t: This is because the more technology is put into the field, the more people are needed to deploy, maintain, and improve it.
lines.cn: 因为投入现场的技术越多，就需要越多的人去部署、维护和改进它。

lines.t: The automation and digitization of the industry is creating a need for different jobs.
lines.cn: 行业的自动化和数字化正在创造对不同岗位的需求。

lines.t: These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence.
lines.cn: 这些岗位包括数据科学家以及自动化和人工智能领域的工程师。

lines.t: The mining companies claim automation and robotics present opportunities to make mining more sustainable and safer.
lines.cn: 矿业公司声称，自动化和机器人技术带来了让采矿更可持续、更安全的机会。

lines.t: Employees will be offered a career that is even more fulfilling and more rewarding.
lines.cn: 员工将获得更有成就感、更有回报的职业。

lines.t: Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology, but they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology.
lines.cn: 工会已接受了新技术引入的不可避免，但对自动化技术的兴起仍持保留意见。

lines.t: Their main concern is the potential impact on remote communities.
lines.cn: 他们主要的担忧是对偏远社区可能造成的影响。

lines.t: As automation spreads further, the question is how these remote communities will survive when the old jobs are eliminated.
lines.cn: 随着自动化进一步扩散，问题在于当旧岗位消失后，这些偏远社区将如何存续。

lines.t: And this may well prove to be the most significant impact of robotic technology in many places around the world.
lines.cn: 而这很可能被证明是机器人技术在世界许多地方最重大的影响。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about traffic accidents in Thailand?

options.B: Their annual death rate is about twice that of the global average.
options.C: They kill more people than any infectious disease.
options.D: Their cost to the nation's economy is incalculable.

questions.cn: 关于泰国的交通事故，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.D: 对超速施加更重的处罚。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: According to the report by the Department of Labor, According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road death rate is almost double the global average.
lines.cn: 根据劳工部的报告、根据官方统计，泰国每年的道路死亡率几乎是全球平均水平的两倍。

lines.t: Thai people know that their roads are dangerous, but they don't know this could easily be changed.
lines.cn: 泰国人知道他们的道路很危险，但他们不知道这其实很容易改变。

lines.t: Globally, road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease.
lines.cn: 在全球范围内，道路事故每年致死的人数超过任何一种传染病。

lines.t: Researchers at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in America put the death toll in 2017 at 1.
lines.cn: 美国健康指标与评估研究所的研究者把 2017 年的死亡人数定为 124

lines.t: 24 million.
lines.cn: 万。

lines.t: According to the institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century.
lines.cn: 据该研究所说，本世纪以来总体死亡人数大致持平。

lines.t: But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries.
lines.cn: 但这掩盖了各个国家的大量变化。

lines.t: In many poor countries, road accidents are killing more people than ever before.
lines.cn: 在许多贫穷国家，道路事故致死的人数比以往任何时候都多。

lines.t: Those countries have swelling, young populations, a fast-growing fleet of cars and motorbikes, and a limited supply of surgeons.
lines.cn: 这些国家人口年轻且不断膨胀，汽车和摩托车数量快速增长，外科医生却供给有限。

lines.t: It is impossible to know for sure because official statistics are so inadequate, but deaths are thought to have risen by 40% since 1990 in many low-income countries.
lines.cn: 由于官方统计极不完善，无法确知，但据认为许多低收入国家的死亡人数自 1990 年以来上升了 40%。

lines.t: In many rich countries, by contrast, roads are becoming even safer.
lines.cn: 相比之下，在许多富裕国家，道路正变得更加安全。

lines.t: In Estonia and Ireland, for example, the number of deaths has fallen by about two-thirds since the late 1990s.
lines.cn: 例如在爱沙尼亚和爱尔兰，死亡人数自 20 世纪 90 年代末以来下降了约三分之二。

lines.t: But the most important and intriguing changes are taking place in middle-income countries, which contain most of the world's people and have some of the most dangerous roads.
lines.cn: 但最重要也最引人关注的变化正发生在中等收入国家，那里汇聚了世界大部分人口，也有一些最危险的道路。

lines.t: According to researchers, in China and South Africa, traffic deaths have been falling since 2000, and in India since 2012.
lines.cn: 据研究者说，在中国和南非，交通死亡人数自 2000 年以来一直在下降，印度则从 2012 年开始下降。

lines.t: And the Philippines reached its peak four years ago.
lines.cn: 菲律宾在四年前达到了峰值。

lines.t: The question is whether Thailand can soon follow suit.
lines.cn: 问题在于泰国能否很快跟进。

lines.t: Rob McKinney, head of the International Road Assessment Program, says that all countries tend to go through three phases.
lines.cn: 国际道路评估项目负责人罗伯·麦金尼说，所有国家往往都经历三个阶段。

lines.t: They begin with poor, slow roads.
lines.cn: 起初是破旧、缓慢的道路。

lines.t: In the second phase, as they grow wealthier, they pave the roads, allowing traffic to move faster and pushing up the death rate.
lines.cn: 第二阶段，随着国家变富，他们把道路铺上路面，让交通更快，推高了死亡率。

lines.t: Lastly, in the third phase, countries act to make their roads safer.
lines.cn: 最后，在第三阶段，国家采取行动让道路更安全。

lines.t: The trick, then, is to reach the third stage sooner, by focusing earlier and more closely on fatal accidents.
lines.cn: 因此，诀窍在于更早地关注致命事故、更紧密地研究它们，从而更快进入第三阶段。

lines.t: How to do that?
lines.cn: 如何做到？

lines.t: The solution lies not just in better infrastructure, but in better social incentives.
lines.cn: 答案不仅在于更好的基础设施，也在于更好的社会激励机制。

lines.t: Safe driving habits are practices which people know they should follow, but often don't.
lines.cn: 安全驾驶习惯是人们知道自己应该遵循、但常常并不遵循的做法。

lines.t: Dangerous driving is not a fixed cultural trait, as some imagine.
lines.cn: 危险驾驶并不是像有些人想象的那样是一种固定的文化特质。

lines.t: People respond to incentives, such as traffic laws, that are actually enforced.
lines.cn: 人们会对真正被执行的激励——比如交通法规——作出反应。
